subject: Telemetry adapter compatibility checklist & QA validation run
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: John Martin <john.martin@datadog.com>, Lena Berg <lena@grafana.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:14:00Z
Subject: Telemetry adapter compatibility checklist & QA validation run

Hi John, Lena —

Following up from last week's partner sync: we want to validate a Redwood telemetry adapter that behaves consistently with Datadog ingestion and Grafana dashboards for common LLM-serving signals (latency/tokens/sec, KV cache hit ratio, model-fallback events). Goal: have a short QA validation run with both your ingestion endpoints to confirm compatibility before we include the adapter in our Partner Integrations catalog.

Attached is a first-pass adapter spec (adapter-spec-draft.pdf) and a short checklist of the integrations we plan to run. High-level asks:
- Confirm Datadog/OTLP ingest compatibility for OTLP traces + metrics over gRPC.
- Confirm Grafana dashboard panel IDs we should target for out-of-the-box mapping.
- Provide a lightweight test harness (or instructions) we can run in our CI to verify events and labels.

Can you confirm the right technical contacts and whether you'd prefer OTLP over HTTP for the test? Also propose 60-minute slots for a tech sync next week — we want Redwoods QA + your ingestion engineer + one product PM.

Thanks — happy to narrow scope if you'd rather start with a smoke test.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Partnerships Manager, Integrations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: adapter-spec-draft.pdf (PDF, 320 KB)
From: John Martin <john.martin@datadog.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Chang <mike@datadog.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T15:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Telemetry adapter compatibility checklist & QA validation run

Thanks Karthik — Luke looped me in. Quick responses inline:

- OTLP over gRPC is preferred for traces and metrics; we support HTTP/JSON but gRPC keeps labels consistent.
- For metric naming, send service.name="redwood-inference" and include attributes: model.name, inference.seq_len, kv_cache_hit (0/1).
- We'll share a minimal sample config: dd-sample-config.yaml (attached).
- I can bring our ingestion QA (Mike Chang) into a quick call to walk through the harness.

Proposed availability: 2026-12-01 14:00 or 2026-12-02 10:00 PT. Which works on your side?

On attachments: please include sample gRPC payloads if you have them — that will speed validation.

Best,
John Martin
Partner Solutions Engineer
Datadog

Attachments: dd-sample-config.yaml (YAML, 4 KB)

Subject: Fwd: Telemetry adapter compatibility checklist & QA validation run

Grace / Soojin — forwarding John (Datadog) for visibility. They prefer OTLP gRPC and sent a sample config (attached).

Action items for Redwood QA/Eng:
- Produce 2 short example payloads: smoke-trace-1 (single inference trace) and load-50k-tokens (batch of synthetic traces).
- Map internal metric names to their requested attributes (service.name/model.name/inference.seq_len/kv_cache_hit).
- Prepare a small canary deployment we can run against Datadog ingest and Grafana dashboards (Grafana mapping TBD).

Let's pick the 12/01 14:00 PT slot if that works for you both. I'll invite after you confirm availability and I'll include Sean from infra for the canary orchestration.

Thanks —
Karthik

Karthik / Grace —

We have a small test harness you can run locally or in CI to validate OTLP gRPC payloads; attaching instructions (dd-test-harness-instructions.md). Two notes:
1) Ensure timestamps are within 5 minutes of ingestion for trace linking.
2) Use monotonic IDs for span.trace_id to avoid sampling collisions on our side.

Joining the call 12/01 14:00 PT. I'll bring one of our ingestion SREs if we run into sampling/scrubbing issues.

Cheers,
Mike Chang
Ingestion QA
Datadog

Subject: Re: Telemetry adapter compatibility checklist & QA validation run — mutual action plan

Thanks everyone — quick summary and next steps after today's prep: 

Mutual action plan:
- Redwood: populate the shared checklist with two payloads (smoke + load), implement dd-sample-config.yaml in our canary branch, and run the harness in CI (assigned: Grace). Target: 2026-12-03 EOD.
- Datadog: validate ingest results and confirm label mapping on your side; provide any scrub rules that would affect span/metric labels. (owner: Mike).
- Both: run the canary against Grafana mapping the panels John called out and capture screenshots for our integration docs. Target: 2026-12-06.

I've attached the spec we started with and the three artifacts Datadog provided. I'll update HubSpot with the exec summary and mark this as a Partner integration validation task (Deal: DD-OBS-2026-824).

If anything blocks the 12/03 target, please flag in the shared doc or ping me directly.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — talk on 12/01.

—Karthik
